decisive_items: pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of his right eyelids and forearm
response.rationale: Elevated CK and creatinine with alcohol/opioid use and right-sided eyelid/forearm induration indicate rhabdomyolysis causing orbital and limb compartment syndrome; the ocular findings are secondary orbital ischemia, not primary CRAO or angle-closure glaucoma.

rejected.why: Ocular ischemia signs are present, but eyelid edema, chemosis, elevated IOP, serous retinal detachment, sub-RPE fluid, and diffuse leakage are not explained by isolated central retinal artery occlusion.
Elevated IOP and mid-dilated pupil are nonspecific; no angle-closure features and the retinal/choroidal findings plus systemic rhabdomyolysis are inconsistent.
